faq: Do I need a website for Search ads?

Yes, or at least a page that explains your offer and has a way to buy or contact you. If your page is weak, we tell you what to change first, because the page decides how many clicks turn into results.
Who pays Google for the clicks?
You do, directly, from your own Google Ads billing. We agree a daily budget before launch, and your price with us covers only the research, build and review.
Can you promise first page placement?
No. Ad position depends on bids, quality and competition, and nobody controls it. We build the campaign so your ads are relevant, then review the real data and improve from there.
Is this the same as SEO?
No. Search ads are paid and start working as soon as they are approved, but stop when you stop paying. SEO builds organic traffic over time and is a separate service.

desc:
Google Search ads campaign setup puts your business in front of people at the moment they type what you sell. Ecom Swift LLC builds the keywords, ads, extensions and tracking in your own Google Ads account, then launches and reviews it.

## What are Google Search ads?

Google Search ads are text ads that appear above or below the results when someone searches a phrase you have chosen. You pay when a person clicks, not when the ad is shown. The big difference from social ads is intent: the searcher has already raised their hand and said what they want.

That makes Search one of the most direct ways to reach buyers, and also one of the easiest places to waste money. A loose campaign can match your ads to searches you never intended, such as free options, jobs or unrelated products, and every click is billed.

## How campaign structure affects cost and quality

Google decides which ad to show by combining your bid with how relevant and useful your ad and landing page are to the search. A tight structure, with each ad group focused on one theme, lets you write ads that echo the exact words people use. That relevance tends to earn better ad positions at a lower cost per click.

Negative keywords work the other way. They tell Google which searches you do not want, so you stop paying for visitors who were never going to buy. A campaign without them often spends its first weeks learning what a few keywords could have prevented.

## What a strong Search campaign includes

- Keyword research based on the phrases your buyers actually type.
- Ad groups built around one theme each, such as one service or product type.
- Responsive search ads with several headlines and descriptions to test.
- Match types chosen on purpose, rather than left at a default.
- A starter list of negative keywords to filter out unwanted searches.
- Sitelink, callout and call extensions that add clickable detail.
- Location and schedule settings that match where and when you serve customers.
- Conversion tracking connected and tested, so results are measurable.
- A bidding approach suited to the amount of data you have.
- A note on what to watch in the first week.

## What we do

We begin with the words. We study your offer, check how people search for it and group related phrases into tight themes. We then write ads that mention those words naturally and promise only what your page delivers.

Next we build the campaign in your account: ad groups, extensions, locations, schedules and negative keywords. We confirm that conversion tracking records calls, form submissions or sales before launch. After launch we review the search terms report, which shows what people actually typed, and add negatives where needed. The Basic package covers one focused campaign with a few ad groups. Standard widens it to two campaigns with extensions, location settings and a week-one review. Premium adds competitor ad research, a bidding and budget plan and a handover call. Extra ad groups, a negative keyword audit and call tracking can be added.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Send searchers to a page that matches their query.
- Review the search terms report during the first weeks.
- Add negative keywords whenever irrelevant searches appear.
- Keep your location settings tight if you serve a local area.
- Give the campaign time to gather data before judging it.

**Avoid:**
- Sending every ad to your home page.
- Bidding on very broad words that attract casual browsers.
- Judging results after two days.
- Running ads when nobody can answer calls or enquiries.
- Expecting Search ads to behave like SEO, which works on a different timeline.

## Who it is for

This service suits a local business, such as a plumber, dentist or lawyer, that wants calls from nearby searchers. It suits an online store selling products that people already search for by name. It also suits a company with an existing campaign that spends steadily but brings in poor enquiries.

## What we need and how to start

Send your website address, your main services or products with the ones you most want to sell, the areas you serve and your target cost per lead or sale if you know it. We need access to your Google Ads account as a manager, and to your site for tracking, never your passwords. You pay Google directly for clicks, and we agree a daily amount with you first. Ad placement depends on competition and quality, so we cannot fix your position, but we build the campaign to compete as well as it can.
